verses.1: And in twelve months, it was Adar. This lasted for thirteen days. During those days, the king’s decree and laws were carried out. On those days, the enemies of the Jews were defeated, and those who ruled over the Jews became hated by them.
verses.2: The Jews gathered in their cities in all the kingdoms of King Ahşverosh, in order to act against their enemies. No one stood before them, as fear paralyzed them among all the nations.
verses.3: And all the workers in the lands, and the blacksmiths, and the weavers, and all those who work for the king, they carry away the Jews, just as Mordecai’s fear fell upon them.
verses.4: For Mordecai was great in the king’s house. And they heard that he was going throughout all the kingdoms, because Mordecai was indeed a great man.
verses.5: And the Jews suffered in every way: they were killed, wounded, and destroyed. They did whatever they wanted to those who hated them.
verses.6: And in Shushan the Great, the Jews were killed, and five thousand men were destroyed.
verses.7: And also Parshandatah, and Dalphon, and Aspatah.
verses.8: And Portha, and Adalyah, and Aridatha.
verses.9: And also Parmashtah, and Arisai, and Ardi, and Vayzatah.
verses.10: The twelve sons of Manasseh, from the tribe of Bnei Midda, killed the Jews. But at that time, they did not send their bodies away.
verses.11: On that day, the list of those being deported from Shushan came before the king.
verses.12: And the king said to Queen Esther at the royal court, “The Jews have been killed. Five thousand men have been destroyed, along with twelve sons of Haman in all the king’s kingdoms. What have they done? What do you want? I will give you what you ask.”
verses.13: And Esther said, “If the king gives good things to the Jews who are in Susa, so that they may follow the laws of today’s day, and if those twelve sons of Haman are hanged on that tree…”
verses.14: And the king said that it should be done as well. So, they gave the law in Shushan, and also twelve sons of the man.
verses.15: And the Jews gathered at Shushan on the fourteenth day of the month Adar. They killed three thousand men in Shushan. But they did not send the bodies away.
verses.16: And the rest of the Jews who were in the countries under the king’s rule, they stood firm and fearless against their enemies. They killed five hundred seventy thousand of them. But in that battle, they did not send any bloodshed.
verses.17: On the thirteenth day of Adar, in the fourteenth year, he made that day a day of eating and joy.
verses.18: And the Jews, who were gathered in Shushan, did this on the thirteenth day of that month. They also did it on the fourteenth day of that month. And on the fifteenth day of that month, they celebrated it as a day of joy and celebration.
verses.19: Therefore, the Jews who live in the cities of the provinces make a day of joy on the fourteenth day of the month Adar. It’s a day of celebration and eating. It’s also a day for giving gifts to each other.
verses.20: And Mordecai wrote down these words, and sent them to all the Jews who were in all the lands under the rule of King Ahasuerus, both those who lived nearby and those who lived far away.
verses.21: To make sure that they are observed on the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and also on the fifteenth day of that same month, every year.
verses.22: In those days, the Jews lived in peace with their enemies. The new year became a time of joy for them, from a time of sorrow to a time of happiness. It was a time for sharing gifts with each other and giving gifts to their ancestors.
verses.23: And the Jews received what they were required to do, as well as what Mordecai had written to them.
verses.24: For the Ammonite, who is a enemy of the Jews, he seeks to destroy all the Jews. He thinks about destroying them and killing them.
verses.25: And when she came before the king, she said to the scribe, “His evil thoughts about the Jews will be brought back to him. He will be hanged for his crimes, along with his sons.”
verses.26: Therefore, they called these days “Purim”. That’s why all the things related to this festival were also named “Purim”. And what happened during those days, and what happened to them…
verses.27: The Jews must keep and accept these laws, both for themselves and for their descendants. They must also accept all the blessings that are given to them. These laws must not be violated during these two days, as they are written down in the scriptures and according to their time, every year.
verses.28: And these days are remembered and celebrated from generation to generation, from family to family, from country to country, and from city to city. These days shall never be forgotten among the Jews, and their memory shall never be extinguished from their descendants.
verses.29: And Esther, the queen of Abihail and Mordecai the Jew, wrote down all the regulations necessary for carrying out this second set of Purim rituals.
verses.30: And he sent letters to all the Jews, from seven hundred and twenty thousand people, from the kingdom of Ahazia. These were words of peace and truth.
verses.31: To endure these days of suffering during the time when the Jewish rebels and Queen Esther endured them. And to endure, for their souls and their descendants, the words of those who were persecuted and their cries.
verses.32: And Esther said, “Let these words of the prophets be preserved and written down in a book.”
